title: Biloxi hotel bands: Johnny Bajon, Sharkey and Joe Loyacano
summary: Sal recalls Biloxi hotel work and overlooked musicians such as Johnny Bajon, Sharkey, and the Loyacano brothers.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Oh, but the one you're talking about, the big hotel years ago, when I was playing in Biloxi, I was playing with, I believe, with Alex Spatic of the Trauma. I played in some way. And Johnny Quattusi, he was a collected dues for the union for 174 in Biloxi. At that time they had the name bands in this hotel here. And Johnny Bajon was playing the band. See Johnny? Nobody gives a guy any credit. He was playing with the best man, Johnny Bajon. I don't know that. He was playing with the band, Joe Lief was playing. Big band, about four volumes in the band, old man. That's the guy Mr. Johnny was, see. Poor Johnny was nothing or nothing. I don't know what happened to him. But I'm telling you, one time, he was the top man. I live in here Sharky. I ring with the brother, I'm in here Sharky. He said, man, you're a band by Johnny. I want you to hear Sharky play. I'm about to do a man in Taunty. He's up there when he was young, he was the head up there, left hand in the handkerchief, playing Panama. You know, all that stuff. I've been here Johnny, the awful man's rag man, up at the Arcadia on the Canale, the burgundy upstairs in 1923, I believe, 22. Johnny, he could play some corn and then he played in Chicago to Chicago theater. He used to do it for the musicians. He built the best, Frank and Masters, you know. See Johnny? He didn't talk. But I know where he played. What about Joe Boycannon? What?
What about Joe Boycannon? Oh, well I see.
A lot of fellas that don't get mentioned at all, wouldn't really play, see. I noticed that. You're talking about which one?
Steve's brother, the one that just died.
We used to go up there on Monday nights and play and sing, you know.
